ENCUT: Test the target energy difference, forces, or stress
Not an upper bound on electron energies; use one validated cutoff consistently across comparative calculations
PREC: Check together with ENCUT, the mesh, and the task
Accurate does not mean every source of error is converged
EDIFF: Check energy changes between electronic steps for the whole calculation cell
Not an error per atom; setting 0 requests a fixed NELM iteration count
EDIFFG: Negative: force norms; positive: energy change between ionic steps
Does not establish adequate sampling in molecular dynamics
LREAL: Real- or reciprocal-space treatment of nonlocal projectors
For larger systems, test the cost and error of Auto
Compare Auto and .FALSE. for the property of interest
ADDGRID: Additional support grid for augmentation charges
Test whether it reduces the relevant force noise
Interpolation issues can occur; do not enable universally without testing
LASPH: Nonspherical gradient contributions within PAW spheres
Check especially for d/f elements, +U, hybrids, and meta-GGA
Keep the setting consistent across calculations used for energy comparisons
KSPACING: Spacing for an automatic mesh when KPOINTS is absent
A smaller value generally produces more k points
Ignored when KPOINTS is present; inspect the mesh actually generated
KGAMMA: Center the automatic mesh on Γ
Use with KSPACING and the crystal symmetry
Does not override the mesh mode in an explicit KPOINTS file
ALGO: Start with a robust algorithm compatible with the method, then benchmark
Fast is not properly supported for hybrids, and VeryFast is unsupported; check method-specific guidance
NELM: Check whether the run stopped at this limit
A larger limit does not fix a faulty structure or persistent oscillations
ISMEAR: Choose for the material and for energies or forces
Positive values are unsuitable for straightforward use in gapped systems; tetrahedra require an appropriate mesh
SIGMA: Test energies and forces together with the k-point mesh
Only Fermi–Dirac smearing has a direct electronic-temperature interpretation
NBANDS: Metals, hybrid functionals, and optics may need more unoccupied bands
A default or ground-state-sufficient count does not establish convergence of excited-state properties
NELECT: Define the charge state relative to the total PAW valence-electron count
Charged periodic systems require attention to the compensating background, finite size, and reference energies
ICHARG: Initialization or fixing of the charge density
11 is commonly used for compatible CHGCAR-based fixed-density steps
A fixed density is not an SCF solution; check orbital-dependent methods separately
ISTART: Choose based on the available compatible WAVECAR
Check the output to confirm a successful read; a filename is insufficient
GGA: Match the intended method and PAW data; PE specifies PBE
One setting does not turn arbitrary inputs into a valid PBE workflow
METAGGA: Check version, PAW, and kinetic-energy-density requirements
Mesh requirements and fixed-density band procedures may differ from GGA
IBRION: Ionic update, MD, or response task
2 is commonly used for conjugate-gradient relaxation; 0 selects MD
Not every positive value means geometry optimization; consult the task-specific documentation
NSW: Maximum ionic or MD step count
Define the task length together with IBRION
Exhausting NSW does not prove relaxation convergence; MD step count does not establish equilibration
ISIF: Stress calculation and allowed cell/atomic degrees of freedom
Distinguish atomic relaxation, volume changes, and shape changes
Do not freely relax a cell containing vacuum; 8 requires VASP 6.4.1+
POTIM: Time step or ionic displacement/step scale
IBRION=0 requires an explicitly chosen suitable time step
Meaning and units depend on IBRION
PSTRESS: External pressure or related pressure term
State the stress sign convention and target boundary conditions
1 kbar = 0.1 GPa; do not tune it to fit lattice constants without a physical basis
ISYM: Consider the structure, initial moments, and distortions being studied
ISYM=0 is not identical to −1; disabling symmetry is not a universal fix
SYMPREC: Check coordinate rounding and genuine small distortions
A loose tolerance can mistake a real distortion for higher symmetry
ISPIN: When magnetism is possible, test several initial MAGMOM patterns
Use LNONCOLLINEAR for noncollinear calculations and check version-specific combination rules
MAGMOM: Initial magnetic moments and magnetic symmetry
One component per atom for collinear spin; three for noncollinear spin
Does not fix the final moments; removing it at a restart may change symmetry
LNONCOLLINEAR: Use vasp_ncl with the correct three-component input
ISPIN=2 is not required to activate it; check version compatibility
LSORBIT: Use vasp_ncl; check magnetization directions and symmetry
Small magnetic-anisotropy energies require strict numerical convergence
SAXIS: Spin quantization axis and spin-coordinate basis
Interpret MAGMOM and output components in the appropriate frame
Does not apply an external magnetic field; changing the axis changes how vectors are interpreted
LDAU: Specify a consistent set of LDAUTYPE, LDAUL, U, and J settings
Define the corrected orbitals and justify the interaction parameters
LDAUTYPE: Select a +U or related linear-response form
2 selects the Dudarev form; define the effective U−J
U and J have different meanings in different forms; literature values are not interchangeable
LDAUL: 2 for d, 3 for f, and −1 for no correction on that species
Follow POTCAR species order; this is not a per-atom list
LDAUU: U or related interaction parameter in the chosen form
Document its source, calculation, or fitting procedure
Consider whether comparing absolute total energies at different U values is meaningful
LDAUJ: J or related interaction parameter in the chosen form
In the Dudarev form, U and J determine U−J
Its meaning differs for LDAUTYPE=3; consult that form's documentation
LMAXMIX: Maximum one-center angular momentum in mixing and charge files
Fixed-density +U commonly needs 4 for d and 6 for f throughout both stages
Raising it later cannot recover information omitted from an earlier file
LWAVE: Save them when needed for restarts or post-processing
If writing is disabled, an old WAVECAR does not belong to the current run automatically
LCHARG: Plan ahead for fixed-density bands or charge analysis
An old CHGCAR may be incompatible with the current structure
LORBIT: Local orbital projections and related outputs
11 is commonly used for angular-momentum-resolved projections
Projections are method-dependent, not unique atomic charges or oxidation states
NEDOS: Number of energy-grid points for the DOS
Set the intended grid with EMIN and EMAX
Increasing it cannot replace more k points or unoccupied bands
EMIN: Lower edge of the DOS and related energy windows
Not automatically a lower bound measured relative to the Fermi energy
EMAX: Upper edge of the DOS and related energy windows
Use with EMIN, NEDOS, and the actual calculated band range
A window beyond the computed unoccupied bands does not create the missing states
LVHAR: State which potential is used, for example in a work-function calculation
Check the LOCPOT reference, vacuum plateau, and dipole correction
LAECHG: Reconstruct and write densities with all-electron features
Choose the reference density required by the chosen Bader workflow
Files represent different components, such as core, atomic-superposition, or converged valence density; do not confuse them
LHFCALC: Use a compatible functional, AEXX, screening, and solver
A single switch does not fully define HSE06
AEXX: Record it with the chosen hybrid-functional form
Changing the fraction changes the method; it is not an ordinary convergence setting
HFSCREEN: Standard HSE06 uses 0.2 with the other required definitions
Arbitrary combinations of GGA/meta-GGA and screening are not supported
IVDW: Record the correction and its pairing with the functional
11 and 12 use different damping; avoid double-counting dispersion
LDIPOL: Include dipole corrections in the potential and forces
Use with IDIPOL, DIPOL, and sufficient vacuum
Not a universal correction for errors in arbitrary charged periodic systems
IDIPOL: Direction for dipole and related electrostatic corrections
Match the surface normal and cell conventions
A mismatch in direction or dimensionality changes the physical interpretation
DIPOL: Reference center for the dipole moment
For surfaces or molecules, often start near an appropriate center of mass
Fractional coordinates, not Å; check the correction region and vacuum placement
IMAGES: Number of calculation images or replicas
In NEB, specify intermediate images with separate endpoint directories
Also used by other multi-replica methods; check the task and directory conventions
SPRING: Spring and NEB treatment between path images
A negative value selects a nudged elastic band in native VASP
A larger value does not guarantee a better path; keep optimizer settings specific to the implementation
MDALGO: Specify with IBRION=0, ISIF, and the thermostat settings
A temperature setting alone does not establish the ensemble or equilibration
TEBEG: Interpret with the velocity initialization, thermostat, and TEEND
Different from electronic SIGMA smearing; instantaneous temperature fluctuates
LANGEVIN_GAMMA: Langevin friction coefficients for atomic degrees of freedom
For MDALGO=3, follow the actual species blocks
Units are ps⁻¹, not fs⁻¹; NpT also needs lattice friction and mass settings
NCORE: MPI ranks cooperating on each band
For pure MPI, benchmark choices for the basis, hardware, and problem
Do not also set NPAR; GPU and relevant OpenMP paths reset it to 1
NPAR: Understand its relationship to NCORE when reading older inputs
Takes precedence over NCORE if both are set; modern tuning generally favors using NCORE
KPAR: Must divide the available MPI ranks; consider the irreducible-k-point workload
Few k points limit the benefit of larger values; specialized algorithms may give it another meaning
